radial_CDF: Midpoint quantile atoms at (k+1/2)/N give sup CDF discrepancy 1/(2N) from the continuous exponential law, also at atom jumps.
For every k, |Rhat_k^2-S_k|<=eta implies {S_k<=t-eta} subset {Rhat_k^2<=t} subset {S_k<=t+eta}. This uses no ordering of the native map.
F(t)=0 below0 and 1-exp(-t/2) above0 is globally 1/2-Lipschitz. The event inclusions plus midpoint discrepancy give D_S<=min(1,1/(2N)+eta/2).
Positive-part projection is1-Lipschitz and S_k>=0. A=max(-2Lhat,0), R_raw=isqrt(A_raw*Q), and R_raw^2<=A_raw*Q<(R_raw+1)^2 give eta=2E_L+2epsilonB+epsilon^2.
radial_BV: Fix all other pairs and current angle. Every exact unclipped stock is c*exp(beta*r), c>0; real beta may have either sign. Baskets and exact average are convex on r>=0.

Each strict basket sublevel is an interval; their intersection I is an interval, including empty/full/unbounded/constant cases. On I, h=discount*(average-strike)^+ is convex, nonnegative, and bounded by C=(H-K)*discount.

Convex nonnegative h<=C has variation at most2C on I. Zero extension adds at most two endpoint jumps, each<=C, including strict endpoint ties. Total variation<=4C. r=sqrt(s) is monotone, so the same bound holds for squared radius.
Integration by parts for probability measures of equal total mass gives |E_native h-E_continuous h|<=TV(h)*sup|F_native-F_continuous|. Endpoint values at atoms must be retained in variation.
angular_BV: For exact unclipped stocks x_i=A_i*c+B_i*s, y_i=-A_i*s+B_i*c, w_i>0, A_i,B_i>=0, A_i^2+B_i^2<=kappa^2<2. Nonconstant basket derivatives are sum(w*y), sum(w*(y^2-x)).
In quadrantI, A_i,B_i<=kappa and the first exact identity has nonnegative right side. At stationarity c*V=s*U and c^2+s^2=1, the next identities give U=c*X,V=s*X with X=sum(w*x)>0.

Thus sum(w*y^2)<=kappa*s*c*(s+c)*X. The circle identities imply sc<=1/2 and s+c<=sqrt2, hence sc(s+c)<=1/sqrt2. Since kappa<sqrt2, every nonconstant quadrantI stationary point has second derivative<0.

QuadrantII derivative is strictly negative and quadrantIV strictly positive unless all coefficients vanish. In quadrantIII x<=0 and sum(w*(y^2-x))>0 for any nonzero vector, so derivative is strictly increasing. There is one maximum/minimum; all-zero and r0 cases are constant.
A zero derivative at0 forces all B_i=0; at pi/2 forces all A_i=0. These one-axis cases are monotone semicircles. No missing endpoint stationary case is assumed away.

Each strict threshold indicator on the circle has TV<=2, including empty/full/constant cases and H=maximum, where one removed point costs2. The exact Asian average has the same positive-weight form, so min(C,discount*(average-K)^+) has TV<=2C.
The product of nt indicators has TV<=2nt; the bounded-product inequality therefore gives payoff TV<=2C(nt+1). A closed finite basket band may have two arcs and TV4; native band transfer remains open.
midpoint_circle: Split the circle in turns into N equal cells. Each cell midpoint integration error is at most cell variation/(2N); sum gives TV_circle/(2N), with exact strict-tie values included. There is no extra2pi probability factor.
The exact+.75 wrapped midpoint grid is a permutation of the same N turn midpoints, and cos(theta+3pi/2)=+sin(theta). The coordinates remain one joint pair, not two independent digital normals.
actual_point_value_BV_convention: Variation uses the actual priced value at every point: both the left-limit to point-value jump and the point-value to right-limit jump count. A strict barrier tie is not replaced by a right-continuous representative.

Decompose a bounded-variation function using open and closed threshold indicators. Against the continuous comparison law, both indicator errors are bounded by D_S, using F(t) and its one-sided limit F(t-). The sum of the absolute jump weights is the actual-point variation.

A singleton removed maximum therefore costs two jumps in circular variation. The angular cell-midpoint bound also retains exact midpoint point values, including singleton ties; no endpoint convention discards an atom that the native grid can price.
hybrid_order: For each original independent raw-input pair, replace radius FIRST, applying radial BV uniformly in fixed angle and other pairs. Then replace that current angle at its now bounded native radius, applying angular BV uniformly in the positive weights contributed by other pairs.

Other pairs may still have unbounded continuous radii because they only change positive weights. Applying the angular lemma before bounding the current radius is forbidden. Sum the joint-pair errors, never divide by scalar coordinates.
